key_insight: FurnitureVLA shows that Vision-Language-Action models can be scaled to real-world, long-horizon bimanual furniture assembly, moving beyond toy tasks and single-arm manipulation. The paper combines simulation, teleoperation, and real-world demonstrations to make complex assembly training and evaluation practical.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of realistic benchmarks, data collection tools, and learning methods for real-scale furniture assembly with two arms. Existing robot assembly work is mostly limited to toy-scale setups or single-arm tasks, which do not capture the complexity of full furniture assembly.
method: Formalizes real-scale bimanual furniture assembly as a long-horizon robot learning task for VLAs.
Builds a scalable simulation pipeline for expert data generation and evaluation.
Develops a VR teleoperation system for single-operator bimanual control to collect high-quality real-world demonstrations.
impact: This work gives AI/ML practitioners a more realistic pathway for training and evaluating robot foundation models on complex manipulation tasks. It can help accelerate progress toward robots that can assemble furniture in the real world with less task-specific engineering.

paper_title: FurnitureVLA: Learning Long-Horizon Bimanual Furniture Assembly with Vision-Language-Action Model
paper_authors: Chenyang Ma, Yue Yang, Radu Corcodel, Siddarth Jain, Andrew Wu
